summary: Tested admin auth + dashboard, public waitlist, removed-price product pages. 18/18 pytest cases passed, full frontend flow (login, wrong password, dashboard tabs, refresh, CSV export, sign out, waitlist on /collection and /products/:slug, regression on 8 routes) all passed. Found and fixed one critical backend bug in brute-force lockout (naive vs aware datetime crash returning 500 instead of 429).
action_items: None blocking. Optional hardening: configure AsyncIOMotorClient with tz_aware=True so all datetimes read from Mongo are timezone-aware (defense in depth beyond the explicit fix applied).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: Mongo client is created without tz_aware=True, so all datetime fields stored (created_at strings are fine since they're ISO strings, but locked_until is a real datetime) come back naive. Fixed locally for locked_until comparison; consider applying tz_aware=True at the client for future-proofing.

admin_login_attempts uses client IP as document _id, but _client_ip trusts the first value of X-Forwarded-For unconditionally — an attacker can spoof XFF to bypass per-IP lockout. Acceptable for showcase site but worth a comment.

ADMIN_PASSWORD is checked via secrets.compare_digest against the raw env value (no hashing). Fine for a single shared showcase password, but worth noting that the password is stored in plaintext in /app/backend/.env.
Admin.jsx (~352 lines) and server.py (~380 lines) are both still well under the 700-line threshold — no split required.
All interactive elements have data-testid attributes; CSV download produces correctly-named file with the proper columns.

rca of the issue: Bug: In server.py admin_login, the lockout-check did `rec['locked_until'] > now` where `now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (tz-aware) and `rec['locked_until']` was read back from Mongo as a naive datetime (motor's default tz_aware=False). After the 5th failed attempt set locked_until, the 6th attempt crashed with `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes` returning HTTP 500 instead of the intended 429 lockout response. Reproduction: POST /api/admin/login 5 times with wrong password from a fresh IP, observe 5th attempt locks out, 6th attempt → 500. Fix applied (server.py lines ~308-314): on read, if locked_until.tzinfo is None, attach timezone.utc before comparison. Verified: subsequent attempts now return 429 with the proper 'Too many attempts. Try again in N minute(s).' detail.
